symptoms: New leaves grow much smaller than normal.
Leaf stalks become very short, making leaves look like they are stuck to the stem.
The plant looks bushy because many small buds grow together.
Flowers may turn into green leafy structures instead of normal blooms.
Fruits are rare, and if they grow, they stay hard and do not ripen properly.
prevention: Remove and destroy any plants that show signs of the disease early on.
Clear out weeds from the Solanaceae family that can carry the disease.
Choose plant varieties that are known to be tolerant to this disease.
practices: Regularly check your field for plants showing signs of the disease.
Pull out and destroy any infected plants immediately to stop the spread.
Control the leaf hopper insects that carry the disease to healthy plants.
